about.title: Los Gatos Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Los Gatos sits at a busy crossing point where SR-17 traffic climbing toward the Santa Cruz Mountains meets local streets like Los Gatos Boulevard, Blossom Hill Road, and SR-85. Public crash records show 119 injury collisions and 146 people injured in the most recent full year, with reports clustering on Friday afternoons as commuters and weekend travelers overlap. Whether you were rear-ended near a Blossom Hill intersection or caught in slow SR-17 merge traffic, the aftermath is rarely simple: medical visits, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster who wants a recorded statement. Our team handles car accident claims in Santa Clara County. We can review the crash, help preserve evidence like dashcam footage or skid patterns, and explain your options before you say anything that could affect your claim. There's no obligation, and we work on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: The clock is running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government vehicle or roadway defect was involved. Talking to an attorney early helps make sure a shorter deadline doesn't quietly pass you by.

items.title: Comparative fault can affect your claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're found partly responsible for a collision — your share of fault simply reduces the amount. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated by the other side's insurer.

items.title: No cap on your non-economic losses
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case. That makes it worth having someone document the full impact of your injuries rather than accepting an early settlement offer.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later, even if you're just trying to be cooperative. Our team can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on SR-17 or SR-85, a state highway?
items.answer: Crashes on state highways can sometimes involve additional considerations, such as road design or maintenance by a state agency, which may carry a shorter claim deadline than the standard two years. It's worth having an attorney look at the specifics of where on SR-17 or SR-85 the collision occurred before you assume the usual timeline applies.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. We provide free case reviews. Our team typically works on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
